2026-11-07.headline: SharePoint site skills guide now details creation, permissions, and lifecycle controls
2026-11-07.overview: The period brought one documentation update for Copilot in SharePoint. The revised guidance explains how site owners manage site skills from Settings > Site skills, including their storage, ownership, permissions, and lifecycle operations.
2026-11-07.adminImpact: Site owners can use the documented management page and controls to administer site skills. No action is required.

keyChanges.title: Site skills management guidance expanded
keyChanges.detail: The Copilot in SharePoint article now documents creating and managing site skills from Settings > Site skills, including uploading, editing, enabling, disabling, copying, restoring, downloading, and deleting them. It also clarifies storage, ownership, and permissions.

2026-11-09.headline: Sensitivity-labeled PDFs gain web annotation in OneDrive and SharePoint in January 2027
2026-11-09.overview: OneDrive for Business and SharePoint on the web are scheduled to let users with editing rights annotate sensitivity-label protected PDFs without removing their labels. Saved files will retain both annotations and protections, with worldwide rollout planned for late January 2027.
2026-11-09.adminImpact: No admin action is required. Administrators should note that the capability applies only to OneDrive for Business and SharePoint and is intended for users with editing rights.

keyChanges.title: Editing rights will include annotation of protected PDFs
keyChanges.detail: Users with editing rights will be able to annotate sensitivity-label protected PDFs on the web without removing the labels. Annotations and protections will be preserved when the file is saved; worldwide rollout is planned for late January 2027.

2026-11-10.headline: Teams events will share OneDrive videos directly without screen sharing
2026-11-10.overview: The period’s main product update is a planned Microsoft Teams events capability that lets organizers and producers share OneDrive videos through “Manage what attendees see.” A separate SharePoint app-bar guidance update adds detail on navigation features, requirements, Teams integration, and rollout timing.
2026-11-10.adminImpact: No action is required for the OneDrive video-sharing rollout, which begins in mid-November 2026. Administrators configuring global navigation should review the updated guidance for permissions, Teams integration, user access expectations, and the possible 24-hour rollout delay.

keyChanges.title: OneDrive video sharing in Teams events
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Teams will let event organizers and producers share videos directly from OneDrive using “Manage what attendees see,” avoiding screen sharing or embedding videos in PowerPoint and supporting smoother, higher-quality playback. Rollout begins in mid-November 2026, with no action required.

keyChanges.title: Global navigation guidance adds feature and rollout detail
keyChanges.detail: The SharePoint app-bar setup page now describes personalized favorites and recents, quick access to Discover, Publish, Build, and OneDrive, and clarifies global-navigation requirements, permissions, Teams integration, and the possible 24-hour rollout delay.
keyChanges.product: SharePoint app bar and global navigation

2026-11-11.headline: App Intelligence access reviews documented alongside revised Trim Versions guidance
2026-11-11.overview: The November 11 period was documentation-led: Microsoft added a SharePoint governance article describing how administrators can prioritize and investigate non-Microsoft application access, and revised Trim Versions guidance with clearer operational limits and procedures.
2026-11-11.adminImpact: Administrators assessing application access can use the new workflow, although availability, roles, licensing, and assessment data depend on the tenant and release; the article requires no action. Before trimming versions, review the What-if guidance: deleted versions bypass the recycle bin and cannot be recovered unless previously backed up.

keyChanges.title: New workflow covers non-Microsoft application access investigations
keyChanges.detail: The new SharePoint article explains how administrators can prioritize and investigate application access using permissions, site reach, behavior evidence, and privileged-access information. Availability, required roles, licensing, and assessment data vary by tenant and release.

keyChanges.title: Trim Versions guidance now emphasizes the 30-day minimum
keyChanges.detail: The revised article identifies SharePoint Administrators as able to queue trim jobs, simplifies What-if and manual-expiration guidance, highlights the 30-day minimum, and removes the previous text about versions created before January 1, 2023.

2026-11-12.headline: App Intelligence guidance now details owner-notification preview and audit-data coverage
2026-11-12.overview: SharePoint had one documentation update: the App Intelligence access-review article now explains its use of application permissions and activity, an owner-notification preview and confirmation workflow, audit-data coverage, and reporting delays.
2026-11-12.adminImpact: Before sending owner notifications, administrators should review the recipients and message content. They should also account for the documented audit-data coverage and reporting delays when interpreting access-review results.

keyChanges.title: App Intelligence access-review guidance expands workflow and reporting details
keyChanges.detail: The updated SharePoint article describes App Intelligence as using application permissions and activity, adds an owner-notification preview and confirmation workflow, and documents audit-data coverage and reporting delays. Administrators should review recipients and message content before sending notifications and consider the stated data coverage when interpreting results.

2026-11-13.headline: SharePoint temporary authentication URLs retire on April 1, 2027
2026-11-13.overview: The main administrator deadline is the retirement of SharePoint temporary authentication URLs, which will break dependent Power Apps and Automate functionality. Separately, new guidance documents a tenant-level control for restricting agentic users from sharing SharePoint and OneDrive content externally.
2026-11-13.adminImpact: Review Power Apps and Automate functionality that relies on SharePoint temporary authentication URLs before April 1, 2027. For agentic sharing, the documented policy is off by default; administrators can enable it through SharePoint Online PowerShell and scope it to all agentic users or users associated with selected application blueprints, including first- or third-party applications.

keyChanges.title: Power Platform dependencies face a retirement deadline
keyChanges.detail: A Microsoft 365 Message Center notice says SharePoint temporary authentication URLs will be retired on April 1, 2027. Power Apps and Automate functionality that relies on these URLs will break when they are retired, so administrators should review those dependencies ahead of the deadline.

keyChanges.title: Tenant policy restricts agentic external sharing
keyChanges.detail: New Microsoft Learn guidance describes a tenant-level policy for SharePoint and OneDrive that blocks agentic users from sharing content with external users. The policy is off by default and can be enabled through SharePoint Online PowerShell for all agentic users or for users associated with selected application blueprints.

2026-11-02.headline: Unified Copilot Search and group-permission governance reporting headline SharePoint administration
2026-11-02.overview: Two Message Center announcements carry the period: SharePoint Online and OneDrive for the web are moving to a unified Copilot Search experience, with preview rollout beginning in mid-October 2026 and general rollout in mid-January 2027; SharePoint’s Data access governance report for group permissions is scheduled to roll out worldwide from late November to early December. A separate Agents and Copilot article now documents the full site-skills management workflow.
2026-11-02.adminImpact: Copilot Search requires minimal organizational action, and users can opt out during preview. Administrators can use the forthcoming report in the admin center to find sites accessible to particular groups and assess access levels, supporting permission reviews and checks for unintended content exposure. Site owners can administer skills from Settings > Site skills using the documented controls; the article states that no action is required.

keyChanges.title: Copilot Search unifies SharePoint Online and OneDrive web search
keyChanges.detail: The updated experience adds natural-language prompts, AI summaries, and filters. The announced schedule places preview rollout from mid-October 2026 and general rollout from mid-January 2027; users can opt out during preview and organizational action is minimal.
keyChanges.product: SharePoint Online and OneDrive for the web

keyChanges.title: Data access governance report adds group-permission visibility
keyChanges.detail: The new report in the SharePoint admin center will help administrators identify sites accessible to specific groups and assess their access levels. Worldwide rollout is scheduled from late November to early December 2026, supporting permission management and efforts to prevent unintended content exposure.

keyChanges.title: Site skills management is documented under Settings > Site skills
keyChanges.detail: The updated article explains how to create and manage site skills, including uploading, editing, enabling, disabling, copying, restoring, downloading, and deleting them. It also clarifies storage, ownership, and permissions, giving site owners a documented management path.

2026-11-09.headline: Agentic-user sharing policy guidance arrives before SharePoint’s temporary-URL retirement
2026-11-09.overview: Two administrator-level issues stand out: Microsoft has documented an off-by-default tenant policy to block external sharing by agentic users, while SharePoint temporary authentication URLs are scheduled for retirement on April 1, 2027, breaking dependent Power Apps and Power Automate functionality. The week also brought opt-in pay-as-you-go billing for storage overages in January 2027, sensitivity-label-protected PDF annotation in late January, and direct OneDrive video sharing in Teams events beginning mid-November. Remaining page edits were largely operational guidance rather than availability announcements.
2026-11-09.adminImpact: Prioritize identifying Power Apps and Power Automate functionality that uses temporary authentication URLs before April 1, 2027. Decide whether to enable and scope the agentic-user policy to all users or selected application blueprints through SharePoint Online PowerShell; it is off by default. If adopting storage-overage billing, arrange the required Azure billing permissions. The PDF and Teams-event updates require no admin action according to their notices.

keyChanges.title: SharePoint temporary authentication URLs retire April 1, 2027
keyChanges.detail: SharePoint temporary authentication URLs will be retired on April 1, 2027. Power Apps and Power Automate functionality that relies on them will break, making dependency identification and remediation a time-sensitive administration task.

keyChanges.title: New guidance documents an off-by-default agentic-user sharing block
keyChanges.detail: A tenant-level policy can block agentic users from sharing SharePoint and OneDrive content with external users. It is off by default and can be scoped to all agentic users or users associated with selected application blueprints through SharePoint Online PowerShell, including first- and third-party applications.

keyChanges.title: Pay-as-you-go billing planned for SharePoint storage overages
keyChanges.detail: An opt-in meter planned for global rollout in January 2027 will charge for SharePoint storage used beyond the included quota. It integrates with Microsoft 365 Archive and requires Azure billing permissions.

keyChanges.title: Protected PDFs will support web annotation without losing labels
keyChanges.detail: From late January 2027, users with editing rights will be able to annotate sensitivity-label-protected PDFs in OneDrive for Business and SharePoint on the web. Saving preserves both the annotations and the protections; the notice requires no admin action.

keyChanges.title: Teams events will support direct OneDrive video sharing
keyChanges.detail: Beginning in mid-November 2026, event organizers and producers can use “Manage what attendees see” to share OneDrive videos directly during Teams events, avoiding screen sharing or PowerPoint embedding for playback. No admin action is required.

2026-11.headline: Unified Copilot Search, agentic-sharing controls and authentication-URL retirement reshape SharePoint administration
2026-11.overview: November paired a broad user-facing rollout with two governance tracks: SharePoint Online and OneDrive for the web are moving to unified Copilot Search, while a newly documented policy can block external sharing by agentic users. Administrators also received an April 1, 2027 deadline for retiring SharePoint temporary authentication URLs, which will break dependent Power Apps and Power Automate functionality. A group-permission governance report and an opt-in storage-overage meter are also scheduled for rollout.
2026-11.adminImpact: Identify Power Apps and Power Automate functionality that relies on temporary authentication URLs before April 1, 2027. During the Copilot Search preview, users can opt out and organizations need minimal action. Decide whether to enable and scope the agentic-user sharing policy through SharePoint Online PowerShell. When available, use the group-permission report for access reviews; adopting the storage-overage meter requires Azure billing permissions.

keyChanges.title: Unified Copilot Search is coming to SharePoint and OneDrive for the web
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft is updating SharePoint Online and OneDrive for the web to a unified Copilot Search experience with natural-language prompts, AI summaries, and filters. The notice sets preview rollout from mid-October 2026 and general rollout from mid-January 2027. Users can opt out during preview, with minimal organizational action required.
keyChanges.product: SharePoint Online and OneDrive for the web

keyChanges.title: SharePoint temporary authentication URLs retire April 1, 2027
keyChanges.detail: SharePoint temporary authentication URLs will be retired on April 1, 2027. Power Apps and Power Automate functionality that relies on these URLs will break when the retirement takes effect, making dependency identification an urgent administrator task.

keyChanges.title: A new policy guide covers agentic-user external sharing
keyChanges.detail: A new SharePoint and OneDrive article documents a tenant-level policy that blocks agentic users from sharing content with external users. The policy is off by default and can target all agentic users or users associated with selected application blueprints through SharePoint Online PowerShell.

keyChanges.title: Group-permission governance reporting is coming to the SharePoint admin center
keyChanges.detail: SharePoint is introducing a Data access governance report that identifies sites accessible to specific groups and shows their access levels. Worldwide rollout is planned from late November through early December 2026, giving administrators a way to investigate permissions and potential unintended exposure.

keyChanges.title: SharePoint storage overages gain an opt-in pay-as-you-go meter
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft is introducing consumption-based billing for SharePoint storage used beyond the included quota. The opt-in capability is scheduled for global rollout in January 2027, integrates with Microsoft 365 Archive, and requires Azure billing permissions.
